questions.question: Why does an AI portfolio need active management?
options: Because quick wins, strategic bets, risk controls, capacity, and learning need to be balanced
questions.explanation: Portfolio management makes tradeoffs visible across initiatives.

questions.question: Which signal is explicitly part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: Capacity conflict is a portfolio signal.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked portfolio plan with controls and rationale
questions.explanation: The artifact supports portfolio triage and steering.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
questions.explanation: Kill criteria help teams stop weak initiatives.

questions.question: When should an initiative receive stronger portfolio controls?
options: When impact, uncertainty, dependencies, or capacity conflicts are high
Only when it is already finished
Only when no stakeholder is involved
Never; portfolios should not be reviewed
questions.explanation: High-risk portfolio items need explicit review and steering.

questions.question: Why are kill criteria useful?
options: They prevent weak pilots from consuming capacity indefinitely
questions.explanation: Kill criteria protect capacity and focus.
